import unittest
from subject import subject_text

class Subject(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_encoded_words(self):
        self.assertEqual(subject_text('=?utf-8?B?5L2g5aW9?='),'你好')
        self.assertEqual(subject_text('=?iso-8859-1?Q?caf=E9?='),'café')
        self.assertEqual(subject_text('=?utf-8?B?5L2g?= =?utf-8?B?5aW9?='),'你好')
        self.assertEqual(subject_text('=?iso-8859-1?Q?caf=E9?= =?utf-8?B?5aW9?='),'café好')
    def test_plain_and_mixed(self):
        self.assertEqual(subject_text('  Ops digest  '),'  Ops digest  ')
        self.assertEqual(subject_text('Re: =?utf-8?B?5L2g5aW9?='),'Re: 你好')
        self.assertEqual(subject_text(''),'')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# mail-subject-unfolding

Behavior contract:
subject_text(value) decodes RFC 2047 encoded words in a mail subject using their declared charset and returns a Unicode string. Leave ordinary text unchanged. Adjacent encoded words are joined according to email.header decoding rules; mixed plain text is retained. Inputs contain valid encoded words and supported charsets.

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.
Use only the runtime standard library. Preserve public interfaces and existing assertions; do not install dependencies or access the network.
